_meta.indication: ZEPOSIA is indicated for the treatment of relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS), to include clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease, and active secondary progressive disease, in adults.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, parallel-group, active comparator-controlled (IFN beta-1a).
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Annualized relapse rate (ARR) over the treatment period.
pivotal_trials.n: N=895 randomized (ZEPOSIA n=447; IFN beta-1a n=448).
pivotal_trials.result: ARR 0.181 (ZEPOSIA 0.92 mg) vs 0.350 (IFN beta-1a); relative reduction 48% (p<0.0001).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, parallel-group, active comparator-controlled (IFN beta-1a); 24-month treatment period.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis.
pivotal_trials.n: N=874 randomized (ZEPOSIA n=433; IFN beta-1a n=441).
pivotal_trials.result: ARR 0.172 (ZEPOSIA 0.92 mg) vs 0.276 (IFN beta-1a); relative reduction 38% (p<0.0001).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=4%): upper respiratory infection (26% vs 23% IFN beta-1a), hepatic transaminase elevation (10% vs 5%), orthostatic hypotension (4% vs 3%), urinary tract infection (4% vs 3%), back pain (4% vs 3%), and hypertension (4% vs 2%). Serious risks include infections, bradycardia/AV conduction delays, and liver injury.
target_moa: Ozanimod is a sphingosine 1-phosphate (S1P) receptor modulator that binds with high affinity to S1P receptors 1 and 5 and blocks the capacity of lymphocytes to egress from lymph nodes, reducing lymphocytes in peripheral blood.

rems.type: A Risk Evaluation and Management Strategy is not necessary to ensure that the benefits of ozanimod outweigh the risks.

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the drug is not the first in its class, the safety profile is similar to other drugs approved for the indication, and the efficacy findings are clear.

description.text: Added indication for treatment of moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis in adult patients

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the use of Zeposia (ozanimod) for the treatment of moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis in adult patients.

summary.text: Standard NDA under section 505(b), approved March 20, 2020 based on two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 active-controlled trials (RPC01-201B and RPC01-301); the initial submission had received a Refuse to File action on 2/23/2018; not referred to an advisory committee; no accelerated approval or expedited-program designations stated.

citations.quote: Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) dated and received March 25, 2019, and your amendments, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Zeposia (ozanimod) capsules, 0.23 mg, 0.46 mg, and 0.92 mg.

The applicant presents the results from two adequate and well-controlled clinical trials (RPC01-201B and RPC01-301) as the basis of support for the effectiveness of ozanimod for the treatment of relapsing forms of MS.
Of note, the initial submission of this NDA resulted in a Refuse to File action on 2/23/2018 because a major active metabolite (RP112273) had not been adequately characterized.
